title: Evaluation of Trusted Debate in LinuxArena
location: Copenhagen, Denmark and Washington DC, USA
team: Team Evaluation of Trusted Debate in LinuxArena
summary: We investigated using Trusted Debate as a trajectory-level monitor in LinuxArena to identify agent trajectories which contained sabotage. Trusted Debate involves using a Defender and Critic model to argue whether a given trajectory contains sabotage before a Judge model provides a final suspiciousness score. In our limited experiments, we show that the Debate framework actually lowers monitor performance compared to a lower-cost baseline, with the Defender in particular muddying the water and confusing the judge. An ablation which replaced the Defender prompt with a simple deferral to the Critic response recovers performance to be competitive with the baseline, suggesting that the Defender actively degrades monitoring performance.
reviews:
Good analysis. I'm of the opinion that it's hard to justify Trusted Debate, since it's effectively a fancy monitor in a trench coat, and risks rigidity. Some minor critiques that come to mind:

- Perhaps the work would have been more interesting & novel if applied to the live, per-action setting.
- The conclusion's framing is a bit strong.
- It'd be good to clarify why the critic-only variant was provided such a different prompt than A / B variants. The critic>debate result could be purely due to a much better monitor prompt than the ones it is compared to.

Overall, truly impressive work.
Interesting approach with debate., worth publishing a negative result
